result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say the designer is partly right, recommend a simplified mark, a symbol-only favicon and a stitch-out sample, and keep the scope small. B covers the causes more fully: low contrast and gradients in the favicon, fabric pull on knit polos, and the digitizer's role and cost. A gives the clearer quick test, checking the mark in solid black and reversed, and offers to tailor the advice to the actual logo. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say the designer is partly right and recommend a simplified mark, a favicon, and a stitch-out proof, scaled for a small firm. B pins the problem more clearly on the logo itself ('one logo file doing every job') and links narrow gaps filling with thread to the melted lines. B also gives a better quick test: check the mark in one flat color, black on white and reversed, at 16 to 32px. A covers contrast and gradients a bit more explicitly and has a slightly tighter deliverables list.
